chunks: What is arcing?. The question: What is arcing?
An arc is an electrical spark that jumps through air (or another gas) between two conductors that are close but not touching.
The gas heats up and becomes a glowing, conducting plasma. Arcs appear when the voltage across a gap gets high enough, and a common cause is opening a switch on a coil.
Think of the shock you get from a doorknob after walking on carpet. Air is normally an insulator.
But when the electrical push across it gets strong enough, it suddenly breaks down and a spark flows. An arc is the same breakdown, except that it can keep burning.
The analogy has a gap: a static shock is brief, while an arc on a steady (DC) supply can persist because the voltage never passes through zero.
Left of the minimum, the gap is too small for the electrons to ionise enough gas. Right of it, higher pressure or gap needs more voltage.
At atmospheric pressure ( p equals 760 Torr) a 10 µm gap has pd equals 0. 76 Torr·cm: about 300 volts.
A 1 mm gap ( pd equals 76 ) needs about 5 kilovolts by this fit; a measured value for a uniform 1 mm air gap is more like 4–5 kilovolts, consistent with ~3–4 kilovolts/mm.
For very small gaps (below a few µm) the fit isn't reliable and field emission dominates.
Arc: a sustained electrical discharge through a gas, hot and glowing. Breakdown: the moment an insulating gas starts to conduct.
Plasma: gas that has been ionized (charged) so it conducts. Inductive current: current through a coil, which resists stopping.
Snubber: a small circuit that absorbs the spike across a contact.
Air breaks down at roughly 3 million volts per meter in larger gaps. A 1 mm gap therefore needs roughly 3,000 volts to spark.
Now a switch opens in series with a coil carrying 1 amps.
The coil insists on keeping 1 amps flowing, so the voltage across the opening gap climbs until the gap breaks down, and an arc forms.
A diode (a one-way valve for current) across the coil gives the current a path instead, so the gap never sees that voltage.
That is the whole idea: an arc is a gap breaking down, and coils push the voltage high enough to cause it.
"Arcing is a discharge through ionised gas between two conductors, hot plasma that conducts at a low voltage once it's lit.

It starts either from breakdown of a gap by high voltage, or, the common case, when you interrupt current in an inductor: v equals L di over dt drives the opening gap's voltage up until air breaks down, and DC has no zero crossing to put it out.
It erodes contacts and brushes, makes EMI, and can start fires. Fix it by giving the current another path, a flyback diode, RC snubber, TVS, or by using a solid-state switch."
